mainTopic: רבא's teachings about the עולה, and the sources that a פסח and a חטאת brought שלא לשמה are פסול.
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier point: a חטאת does not atone for a מצות עשה as its main job, but it does atone for it on the side. Then come several teachings of רבא. If an עולה was slaughtered שלא לשמה, its blood still may not be sprinkled שלא לשמה. An עולה brought by heirs after the owner died is ruined by שינוי קודש but not by שינוי בעלים, since there is no owner after death. רב פנחס disagrees and holds that the heir is a full owner. רבא also teaches that an עולה is a דורון, a gift to הקב"ה. A ברייתא of רבי שמעון supports this: the חטאת goes first like a lawyer, and the עולה follows as a gift. The גמרא then returns to the משנה and finds פסוקים showing that a פסח brought with the wrong intention, whether for the wrong type of קרבן or the wrong owner, is פסול. It shows this is essential and covers every עבודה, explains the word 'הוא' by contrasting פסח with אשם, and begins finding the sources for חטאת, starting with שחיטה and קבלה.

steps.title: A חטאת atones for a positive מצוה only on the side
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the earlier question: a חטאת does not atone for an עשה as its main purpose, but it does atone for it on the side.
steps.simpleTranslation: It does not atone from its essence, but it does atone incidentally.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes an earlier discussion by explaining how a חטאת relates to a מצות עשה. It atones for it, but only as a side effect.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חטאת is brought for a לא תעשה, so atoning for an עשה is not its real job. The answer splits the question in two: it is not the main purpose, but some atonement still happens along the way.

keyTerms.meaning: The essence or fixed main purpose of something
Something on the side, incidental
It atones

steps.whatToRemember: A חטאת atones for an עשה only on the side, not as its main purpose.

phrases.english: From its essence it does not atone,
phrases.notes: Picture the main job of the חטאת versus something it does along the way.

phrases.english: incidentally it does atone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes a discussion from the previous section of the daf.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction: main purpose versus side effect
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Either a חטאת fully atones for an עשה, or it does not atone for it at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: It does not atone for an עשה as its essence, but it does atone incidentally.

steps.title: After a wrong-intent slaughter, do not sprinkle with wrong intent
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that if an עולה was slaughtered שלא לשמה, the blood still may not be sprinkled שלא לשמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: A burnt offering that one slaughtered not for its sake: it is forbidden to sprinkle its blood not for its sake.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic with a ruling from רבא. One mistake in the service does not permit more mistakes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might think that once the שחיטה was done with the wrong intent, the קרבן is already 'spoiled', so the rest does not matter. רבא says no. The זריקה must still be done with the right intent.

keyTerms.meaning: Burnt offering
Not for its own sake, with the wrong intent
To sprinkle its blood on the מזבח

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying the first mistake can be undone. He is saying you may not add a second mistake on purpose.

phrases.english: And Rava said:
A burnt offering that one slaughtered not for its sake –
it is forbidden to sprinkle its blood not for its sake.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, unrelated to the חטאת discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even after an שלא לשמה slaughter, the זריקה must not be done שלא לשמה.

steps.title: First reason: a verse about keeping your word
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives two possible reasons for רבא's rule. The first is the פסוק 'מוצא שפתיך תשמר'.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say a verse; if you want, say a logical reason. If you want, say a verse: 'That which comes out of your lips you shall keep, etc.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says רבא's rule can be supported in two ways, a פסוק or logic. It begins with the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The owner promised this animal as an עולה, so the whole service must match that promise. One part going wrong does not cancel the duty to keep the rest of the promise.

keyTerms.meaning: If you want, say; it introduces one of two possible reasons
A verse
Keep what comes out of your lips; keep your vow

phrases.english: If you want, say a verse,
if you want, say a logical reason.
If you want, say a verse:
"That which comes out of your lips you shall keep, etc."
phrases.notes: דברים 23:24. The "etc." means the rest of the פסוק, which the גמרא doesn't quote here.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא קְרָא, אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא סְבָרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a source for רבא's ruling in step 2.
steps.raayaObject: The ban on sprinkling the blood שלא לשמה after an שלא לשמה slaughter.

steps.title: Second reason: one change does not justify more changes
steps.stepSummary: The second reason is logic: just because he changed once, should he keep on changing? This was already explained at the start of the פרק.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say a logical reason: because he deviated with it, etc., as at the beginning of the chapter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the second support for רבא, a logical argument, and points back to where it was already explained.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The logic is that one deviation is no excuse for another. The גמרא gives only the opening words and the reader fills in the rest from the start of the פרק.

keyTerms.meaning: Logical reasoning
That he deviated with it, did it differently than required
As at the beginning of the chapter

steps.whatToRemember: רבא's rule rests on a פסוק (keep your vow) and on logic (one mistake does not permit another).

phrases.english: If you want, say a logical reason:
because he deviated with it, etc.,
phrases.notes: The "etc." stands for the rest: should he go on and deviate with it more?

phrases.english: as at the beginning of the chapter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, independent support alongside the פסוק in step 3.
steps.raayaObject: The ban on continuing the service שלא לשמה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Logic: one deviation does not permit another, as at the start of the פרק.

steps.title: An עולה brought after the owner's death
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that an עולה brought after the owner died does not count if slaughtered for a different type of קרבן. It is fine if slaughtered for a different person, since a dead owner is no longer an owner.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: A burnt offering that is brought after death: if one slaughtered it with a change of offering type, it is unfit; with a change of owner, it is fit, because there is no owner after death.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ruling from רבא about an עולה brought after its owner has died. It treats the two kinds of wrong intent differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שינוי קודש still matters because the animal is still an עולה. שינוי בעלים only hurts when there is an owner to lose out, and after death there is no owner in the legal sense, so that intent changes nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: After death, here meaning after the owner died
Wrong intent about the type of offering
Wrong intent about the owner
Unfit, here meaning it does not count
Fit, valid

steps.confusionAlert: Here פסולה means the קרבן does not count for the owner's obligation, so the heirs must bring another one.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that שינוי בעלים depends on there being a real owner, while שינוי קודש depends on the קרבן itself.
steps.whatToRemember: After the owner dies, only שינוי קודש affects the עולה. שינוי בעלים does nothing because there is no owner.

phrases.english: And Rava said:
A burnt offering that is brought after death:
phrases.notes: He means the owner set it aside, then died, and now his heirs bring it.

phrases.english: if one slaughtered it with a change of offering type, it is unfit;
with a change of owner, it is fit,
because there is no owner after death.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רָבָא: עוֹלָה הַבָּאָה לְאַחַר מִיתָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new statement of רבא, joined to the previous one by 'ואמר רבא'.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For an עולה brought after the owner's death, שינוי קודש makes it not count, but שינוי בעלים leaves it valid, since there is no owner after death.

steps.title: רב פנחס: an offering still has an owner after death
steps.stepSummary: רב פנחס בריה דרב אמי rules that a קרבן still has an owner after the original owner dies, meaning the heir.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב פנחס, son of רב אמי, says: there is an owner even after death.
steps.whatsHappening: A new אמורא disagrees with רבא's ruling from the last step. He says the heir counts as the owner of the קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said a dead owner is no longer an owner, so slaughtering the עולה for a different person does not ruin it. רב פנחס holds the opposite: the heir steps in as the owner. That means slaughtering it for the wrong person could be a real problem.

keyTerms.meaning: Owner of the קרבן, the one it is brought for
After death
Heir (the one the גמרא means by 'owner' here)

steps.confusionAlert: רב פנחס is arguing with רבא from step 5. Don't mix up the two opinions: רבא says no owner after death, while רב פנחס says there is one.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַב פִּנְחָס בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אַמֵּי אָמַר:
phrases.english: And Rav Pinchas, son of Rav Ami, says:
There is an owner after death.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב פִּנְחָס בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אַמֵּי אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an opposing view to רבא's ruling in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A קרבן has an owner (the heir) even after the original owner's death.

steps.title: רב אשי asks how far Rav Pinchas means this
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי asks whether the heir is a full owner who must bring a new עולה, or whether the עולה only helps the heir by atoning for his עשה violations.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said to רב פנחס son of רב אמי: Does the master mean exactly that there is an owner after death, so the heir must bring another עולה if it was slaughtered for someone else? Or perhaps you only mean that if the heir has several positive commandments he failed to do, the עולה atones for them?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי is asking a clarifying question. He wants to know how strongly רב פנחס means his rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two ways to read רב פנחס. Strong reading: the heir is a true owner, so slaughtering for someone else ruins the קרבן and a new one is needed. Weak reading: the heir just gets the benefit of atonement for his missed עשה, but the קרבן is not ruined if slaughtered for someone else.

keyTerms.meaning: Exactly, precisely, in the full sense
Or perhaps
A positive commandment (a מצוה to do something)
It atones

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אָשֵׁי לְרַב פִּנְחָס בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אַמֵּי:
phrases.english: Rav Ashi said to Rav Pinchas, son of Rav Ami:
Is the master saying it exactly,
that there is an owner after death,
and he needs to bring another burnt offering?
Or perhaps
that if there are several positive commandments on him,
phrases.notes: He means positive מצוות the heir failed to keep.

phrases.english: it atones?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how strongly to read רב פנחס's ruling in step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the heir a full owner (requiring a new עולה if slaughtered for someone else), or does the עולה merely atone for the heir's missed עשה?

steps.title: רב פנחס: I mean it exactly
steps.stepSummary: רב פנחס answers that he means it fully: the heir is a real owner.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I mean it exactly.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פנחס answers רב אשי's question. He picks the strong reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So the heir is a full owner. If the עולה is slaughtered for someone else, it does not count, and the heir must bring another one. This is a clear argument with רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: I am saying

steps.whatToRemember: רבא: no owner after death, so slaughtering for a different person is fine. רב פנחס: the heir is a full owner, so slaughtering for a different person means a new עולה is needed.

phrases.english: He said to him:
I am saying it exactly.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אשי's question from step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The strong reading: the heir is a full owner and must bring another עולה if it was slaughtered for someone else.

steps.title: רבא: a burnt offering is a gift
steps.stepSummary: רבא teaches that an עולה is a דורון, a gift to הקב"ה, and not mainly for atonement.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא says: an עולה is a gift.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another teaching of רבא. He says the main idea of an עולה is a gift.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier we saw that an עולה atones for an עשה. רבא now says that atoning is not its main job. Mainly it is a gift brought to win favor with הקב"ה.

keyTerms.meaning: A gift
Burnt offering, burned completely on the מזבח

phrases.english: And Rava says:
A burnt offering is a gift.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new teaching of רבא, connected to the theme of what an עולה does.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An עולה is essentially a gift to הקב"ה, not mainly an atonement.

steps.title: Proof that a burnt offering must be a gift
steps.stepSummary: רבא proves his point: without תשובה the קרבן is rejected, and with תשובה the person is already forgiven, so the עולה must be a gift.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If there is no תשובה, then 'the sacrifice of the wicked is an abomination!' And if there is תשובה, a ברייתא teaches: if someone broke a positive commandment and did תשובה, he does not move from there until he is forgiven! So learn from this that it is a gift.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא shows why an עולה can't be mainly for atonement. He checks both possible cases and shows that atonement doesn't fit either one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Case 1: the person did not do תשובה. Then his קרבן is disgusting to הקב"ה, so it can't atone. Case 2: he did do תשובה. Then a ברייתא says he is forgiven right away for an עשה, so the עולה is not needed for atonement. The only option left is that the עולה is a gift.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? How do we picture it?
Repentance
Abomination, something disgusting
Learn from this, conclude from it

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that even after a person is forgiven, he still brings an עולה, like bringing a gift to make peace after being forgiven.

phrases.english: What are the circumstances?
phrases.notes: In what case would an עולה atone for an עשה?

phrases.english: If there is no repentance,
'The sacrifice of the wicked is an abomination!'
phrases.notes: משלי 21:27

phrases.english: And if there is repentance,
isn't it taught in a ברייתא:
If one violated a positive מצוה and repented,

phrases.aramaic: לֹא זָז מִשָּׁם עַד שֶׁמּוֹחֲלִים לוֹ!
phrases.english: he does not move from there until he is forgiven!
Rather, learn from this
that it is a gift.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves רבא's statement from step 9.
steps.raayaObject: That an עולה is a gift and not mainly for atonement.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The פסוק 'זבח רשעים תועבה' (no תשובה) and the ברייתא that one who repents from an עשה is forgiven immediately (with תשובה).
steps.whatToRemember: No תשובה means the קרבן is rejected. With תשובה he is already forgiven. So the עולה is a gift.

steps.title: Memory aid for רבא's statements
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a סימן, a short memory aid, for the series of רבא's statements in this section, starting on the previous amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: A sin offering atones for whom, a burnt offering, after, gift: this is a memory aid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the section with a memory aid. Each word reminds us of one of רבא's teachings, in order.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words point to רבא's statements: חטאת על מי מכפר (רבא's earlier statements on the previous amud about a חטאת, including a חטאת slaughtered for someone obligated in an עולה, and what it atones for), עולה (an עולה slaughtered שלא לשמה), לאחר (an עולה after the owner's death), and דורון (an עולה is a gift). It is just a tool to remember the order.

keyTerms.meaning: A memory aid, a short phrase to help remember a list
Sin offering

phrases.english: A sin offering atones for whom,
phrases.notes: Each word hints at one of רבא's teachings on this page, in the same order.

phrases.english: burnt offering, after, gift:
a mnemonic.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Wraps up the series of רבא's statements with a memory aid.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A memory aid listing רבא's teachings in order: חטאת, עולה שלא לשמה, עולה after death, עולה as a gift.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רבא: רבי שמעון's question
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that backs up רבא's idea that an עולה is a gift. It opens with רבי שמעון asking why a חטאת is brought.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא also teaches this. רבי שמעון said: Why does a חטאת come?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to support what רבא just said. This line only opens the ברייתא with רבי שמעון's question, and the answer comes in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words תניא נמי הכי tell us that an older teaching agrees with רבא. רבי שמעון's question sounds strange at first, and the גמרא will deal with that right away.

keyTerms.meaning: It is also taught this way in a ברייתא, a supporting source
Sin offering

phrases.english: It is also taught this way:
phrases.notes: This backs up רבא's statement from steps 9 and 10, that an עולה is a gift.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon said:
Why does a sin offering come?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings outside support for רבא's דורון teaching from steps 9 and 10
steps.raayaObject: רבא's claim that an עולה is a דורון

steps.title: The question seems obvious: a חטאת atones
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא breaks in: why ask why a חטאת comes? Everyone knows it comes to atone.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why does it come?! To atone, of course!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא interrupts the ברייתא to point out that רבי שמעון's question seems to have an obvious answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone knows a חטאת brings atonement, so asking its purpose seems pointless. This pushes the גמרא to reread what רבי שמעון really meant.

keyTerms.meaning: To atone, to bring forgiveness

phrases.english: Why does it come?!
To atone!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of רבי שמעון's question
steps.kashyaTarget: The wording of רבי שמעון's question in step 12
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The purpose of a חטאת is plainly atonement, so the question makes no sense as worded.

steps.title: The חטאת comes first like a lawyer, then the gift
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון really asked why the חטאת comes before the עולה. Like a lawyer who wins the king over first, the חטאת atones, and then the עולה enters as a gift.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, why does the חטאת come before the עולה? It is like a lawyer who goes in to the king. Once the lawyer has won the king over, the gift is brought in after him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that רבי שמעון's real question was about order: why the חטאת is offered before the עולה. He answers with a short parable about a lawyer and a gift.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חטאת is the lawyer that gets the person forgiven. Only after that does the עולה come in, and it comes as a gift (דורון), not for atonement. This is exactly רבא's point.

keyTerms.meaning: An advocate or lawyer who pleads before the king
Appeased, won over
A gift
Burnt offering

steps.whatToRemember: The חטאת atones first, like a lawyer, and then the עולה follows as a gift to הקב"ה. This supports רבא.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי שמעון is not asking why a חטאת exists. He is asking why it is offered before the עולה.

phrases.english: Rather, why does it come before a burnt offering?
It is like a lawyer who goes in to the king,
once the lawyer has won him over, in comes
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets are the corrected wording; some versions don't have them.

phrases.english: the gift after him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by rereading רבי שמעון's question
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the question, so it asks about order rather than purpose
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי שמעון was asking what a חטאת is for
steps.terutzMaskana: He was asking why the חטאת comes before the עולה, and the answer shows the עולה is a gift
steps.whyThisMatters: It gives a source in a ברייתא for רבא's view that an עולה is a דורון.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: where do we learn this about the פסח?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the משנה, which says that offerings brought שלא לשמה are valid except for the פסח and the חטאת. It asks for the source for the פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: except for the פסח and the חטאת. Where do we learn this about the פסח?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the side discussion and returns to the משנה. It asks for the source that a פסח brought for the wrong purpose is invalid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Most offerings stay valid when brought שלא לשמה, so the פסח is an exception that needs a source. This sets up the derivation from a פסוק in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Except for
The Paschal offering
From where do we know this?

phrases.english: Except for the Pesach offering and the sin offering, etc.
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה, which says offerings brought for the wrong purpose are valid except for these two.

phrases.english: The Pesach offering: from where do we know?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side discussion about רבא and returns to the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source showing that a פסח brought שלא לשמה is invalid

steps.title: The פסוק: every action must be for the sake of the פסח
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says 'and you shall make a פסח'. This teaches that every action done with the offering must be for the sake of a פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'Observe the month of spring and make a פסח.' This teaches that all its actions must be done for the sake of a פסח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק. The word 'make' teaches that every step of the offering must be done as a פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ועשית ('and you shall make') is read as covering all the actions (עשיותיו) of the offering. So each step, such as the slaughtering, must be done with the פסח in mind. If not, the offering is invalid.

keyTerms.meaning: And you shall make (offer)
All its actions, meaning the steps of the offering
For the sake of

phrases.english: As it is written:
"Observe the month of spring
and make a Pesach offering"
phrases.notes: דברים 16:1

phrases.english: meaning that all its actions should be
for the sake of a Pesach offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק 'ועשית פסח' teaches that all actions must be done for the sake of a פסח

steps.title: What about having the wrong owner in mind?
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק covers thinking of the wrong kind of offering. The גמרא asks for a source that thinking of the wrong owner also makes a פסח invalid.
steps.simpleTranslation: We found a source for a change in the kind of offering. Where do we learn that a change in the owner is also a problem?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says the פסוק covers one kind of wrong intent, and it now asks for a source for a second kind. This sets up the next derivation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two ways to bring an offering שלא לשמה: thinking of a different kind of offering (שינוי קודש), or thinking of a different owner (שינוי בעלים). The פסוק so far only proves the first, so the גמרא needs a source for the second.

keyTerms.meaning: We have found
Thinking of a different kind of offering
Thinking of a different owner

phrases.english: We have found a source for changing the kind of offering;
changing the owner: from where do we know?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַשְׁכְּחַן שִׁינּוּי קוֹדֶשׁ, שִׁינּוּי בְּעָלִים מְנָלַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the source from step 16 and points out it covers only one kind of wrong intent
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that a פסח slaughtered for the wrong owner is invalid

steps.title: A second פסוק teaches the rule about the owner
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'ואמרתם זבח פסח הוא' is not needed for the wrong kind of offering, so it is applied to the wrong owner.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And you shall say: It is the sacrifice of פסח.' This means the slaughter must be for the sake of a פסח. We already know the rule about the wrong kind of offering, so use this פסוק to teach the rule about the wrong owner.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 17 with a פסוק that teaches the rule about the owner.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק on its own says the slaughter must be for the sake of a פסח, which sounds like the rule about the type of offering. That rule was already learned in step 16, so this פסוק would be extra. An extra פסוק is used to teach something new, and here it teaches that a פסח must also be brought for the right owner.

keyTerms.meaning: Slaughtering the animal
Changing the type of offering, for example thinking of it as a different קרבן
Changing the owner, meaning thinking of it as belonging to someone else
'If it is not needed for this matter': when a פסוק is extra for one topic, it is applied to another

phrases.english: As it is written: 'And you shall say: It is the sacrifice of פסח'
phrases.notes: שמות 12:27

phrases.english: that the slaughter must be for the sake of a פסח;
if it is not needed for the matter of changing the type of offering,
phrases.notes: That rule was already learned from 'and you shall make a פסח' back in step 16.

phrases.english: apply it to the matter of changing the owner.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the request in step 17 for a source about the wrong owner.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'ואמרתם זבח פסח הוא' is extra for the rule about the type of offering, so it teaches the rule about the owner.

steps.title: Is this requirement essential?
steps.stepSummary: We know it is a מצוה to have the right intentions, but how do we know the offering is invalid without them?
steps.simpleTranslation: We found a source that this is a מצוה. From where do we know that it is essential, so that without it the offering is invalid?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a follow-up question. The פסוקים so far show the correct way to bring a פסח, but do they show the offering is invalid if it was done wrong?
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two levels to a rule. The first is למצוה, the proper way to do it. The second is לעכב, meaning it is essential and without it the offering is invalid. The משנה said a פסח שלא לשמה is invalid, so the גמרא needs a source for that second, stronger level.

keyTerms.meaning: 'We have found' (a source)
As the proper way to do it, ideally
Essential, so that the offering is invalid without it
'From where do we know?'

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up למצוה and לעכב. Something can be the right way to do a מצוה and still not ruin the offering if it was skipped. The גמרא wants proof that for a פסח, the wrong intention really does make it invalid.

phrases.english: We have found a source for the מצוה,
that it is essential, from where do we know?
phrases.notes: 'Essential' means that if it is missing, the פסח is invalid, and not just done less than ideally.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a stronger source after the sources in steps 16 and 18.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that the wrong intention makes the פסח invalid, and not only that the right intention is a מצוה.

steps.title: The פסוק 'וזבחת פסח' makes it essential
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'וזבחת פסח לה׳ אלהיך' shows the requirement is essential.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'And you shall sacrifice the פסח to ה׳ your God, and so on.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that another פסוק about the פסח teaches that this requirement is essential.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah tells us again to sacrifice the animal as a פסח. Repeating the instruction shows that it is essential, so a פסח without the right intention is invalid.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And you shall sacrifice'
'And so on': the פסוק continues

phrases.english: The פסוק says:
'And you shall sacrifice the פסח to Hashem your God, and so on.'
phrases.notes: דברים 16:2

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר קְרָא: וְזָבַחְתָּ פֶּסַח לַה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 19's question about what makes the requirement essential.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra instruction 'וזבחת פסח' shows the requirement is essential.

steps.title: רב ספרא says this פסוק is needed for something else
steps.stepSummary: רב ספרא objects that 'וזבחת' is already used for רב נחמן's teaching.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ספרא challenges this: Does this 'and you shall sacrifice' come to teach this? It is needed for the teaching of רב נחמן.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ספרא attacks the answer of step 20. He says the פסוק is already being used for a different teaching, which the גמרא is about to quote.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A פסוק that is fully used for one teaching cannot easily be used for another. If 'וזבחת' is needed for רב נחמן's rule, then it is not available to show that the right intention is essential. So the question of step 19 needs a new answer, which רב ספרא gives in step 23.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Objects to it': a strong challenge from an אמורא
'Does it come for this?'
'It is needed for' another teaching

phrases.english: רב ספרא objects to it:
Does this 'and you shall sacrifice' come for this?!
This is needed for the teaching of רב נחמן –

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the source given in step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: Using 'וזבחת פסח' to show the right intention is essential.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק is already used for another teaching, so it cannot also teach this rule.

steps.title: רב נחמן's teaching: a leftover פסח becomes a שלמים
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק mentions cattle, which cannot be a פסח, so it teaches that a leftover פסח is brought as a שלמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: From where do we know that a leftover פסח is brought as a שלמים? Because it says: 'And you shall sacrifice the פסח to ה׳ your God, flock and herd.' But a פסח comes only from sheep and goats! From here we learn that a leftover פסח goes to an offering that can come from both flock and herd. And what is that? A שלמים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רב נחמן's teaching to back up רב ספרא's challenge. It shows exactly how the פסוק 'וזבחת' is already being used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says a פסח can come from 'flock and herd', but a real פסח can only be a sheep or a goat. So the פסוק must be talking about what happens to a leftover פסח: it is brought as a קרבן that can come from cattle too, which is a שלמים. Since the פסוק is used up this way, רב ספרא's question stands for now.

keyTerms.meaning: A leftover פסח: an animal set aside as a פסח that was not offered as one
A peace offering, which may come from sheep, goats, or cattle
Flock (sheep and goats) and herd (cattle)
Lambs and goats, the only animals allowed for a פסח

steps.whatToRemember: רב ספרא argues that 'וזבחת פסח... צאן ובקר' is already used to teach that a leftover פסח is brought as a שלמים. So it seems the פסוק cannot also teach that the right intention is essential for a פסח.
steps.whyThisMatters: This teaching is the source for the practical rule that a leftover פסח is brought as a שלמים. It also reopens the question of what makes the intention essential, which רב ספרא answers in step 23.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ:
phrases.english: As רב נחמן said that רבה בר אבוה said:
From where do we know that a leftover פסח is offered as a שלמים?
phrases.notes: A 'leftover פסח' is an animal set aside for the פסח that ended up not being used for it.

phrases.english: As it is said: 'And you shall sacrifice the פסח to Hashem your God,
flock and herd' –
phrases.notes: 'Herd' means cattle. That is the clue, because a פסח is never brought from cattle.

phrases.aramaic: וַהֲלֹא אֵין פֶּסַח בָּא אֶלָּא מִן הַכְּבָשִׂים וּמִן הָעִזִּים!
phrases.english: But a פסח comes only from lambs and from goats!
From here we learn that a leftover פסח

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁיְּהֵא לְדָבָר הַבָּא מִן הַצֹּאן וּמִן הַבָּקָר,
phrases.english: should go to something that comes from the flock and from the herd,
And what is that? A שלמים.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the teaching that step 21 said the פסוק is needed for.
steps.raayaObject: רב ספרא's claim that 'וזבחת' is already used for another teaching.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב נחמן in the name of רבה בר אבוה: 'צאן ובקר' teaches that a leftover פסח is brought as a שלמים.

steps.title: רב ספרא assigns each verse a new job
steps.stepSummary: רב ספרא gives each פסוק its own job: 'וזבחת' teaches רב נחמן's rule, 'שמור' teaches the מצוה about the wrong kind of offering, 'ואמרתם' teaches the מצוה about the wrong owner, and 'הוא' makes both essential.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב ספרא said: 'And you shall sacrifice the פסח' is for רב נחמן's teaching. 'Observe the month of spring' teaches a מצוה about not changing the type of offering. 'And you shall say, it is the sacrifice of פסח' teaches a מצוה about not changing the owner. The word 'it is' makes the rule essential in both cases.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ספרא answers his own objection by giving every פסוק a separate job, so nothing is used twice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this, 'וזבחת' was supposed to show the rule is essential, but it is already used for רב נחמן. Now 'שמור' covers the wrong kind of offering and 'ואמרתם' covers the wrong owner, but only as a מצוה. The single word 'הוא' then makes both requirements essential, so the offering is פסול without the right intention.

keyTerms.meaning: Changing the type of offering in one's mind, for example slaughtering a פסח as if it were a different offering
Slaughtering with the wrong owner in mind
Essential; without it the offering does not work
Required as a מצוה, but not essential to the offering's validity
'It is'; a word in the פסוק that shows the rule is essential

steps.whatToRemember: Each פסוק now has one job. 'שמור' covers the wrong kind of offering, 'ואמרתם' covers the wrong owner, and 'הוא' makes both of them essential.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two levels. 'שמור' and 'ואמרתם' by themselves only teach a מצוה. It is the word 'הוא' that turns both into a requirement that makes the offering פסול.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Safra said:
"And you shall sacrifice the Paschal offering" is for the teaching of Rav Nachman;
phrases.notes: רב נחמן's rule was in the previous step: a leftover פסח is brought as a שלמים.

phrases.english: "Observe the month of spring"
phrases.notes: דברים 16:1

phrases.english: teaches a מצוה regarding a change of offering;
phrases.notes: Literally 'a מצוה with a change of offering.' He means there is a מצוה not to treat it as a different offering.

phrases.english: "And you shall say: It is the sacrifice of Passover"
phrases.notes: שמות 12:27

phrases.english: teaches a מצוה regarding a change of owner;
"It is" teaches that it is essential
both here and there.
phrases.notes: In both cases: the wrong kind of offering and the wrong owner.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves רב ספרא's objection that 'וזבחת' was already taken, by assigning each פסוק a different job.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassignment of פסוקים so that no פסוק is used twice
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'וזבחת' was needed to show the rule is essential, which clashed with רב נחמן's use of it.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'וזבחת' teaches רב נחמן's rule. 'שמור' and 'ואמרתם' teach the מצוה for each kind of change, and 'הוא' makes both essential.

steps.title: What about the other sacrificial services?
steps.stepSummary: The source found so far covers only slaughtering. The גמרא asks how we know the other עבודות must also be done with the right intention.
steps.simpleTranslation: We have found a source for slaughtering. How do we know it for the other services?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices that the פסוקים only speak about slaughtering. It asks for a source for the other עבודות, setting up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב ספרא, what makes the intention essential is the word 'הוא' in 'זבח פסח הוא', and that פסוק speaks about slaughtering. The other עבודות, such as receiving the blood, carrying it and throwing it, are not mentioned there. So the essential rule might seem to apply only to slaughtering.

keyTerms.meaning: Slaughtering the offering
The other sacrificial services, such as receiving, carrying and throwing the blood
From where do we know?

phrases.english: And we have found a source for slaughter;
from where do we derive the other services?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the derivation from slaughtering to the other עבודות.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that the other עבודות also need the right intention

steps.title: Once it was revealed for one, it was revealed for all
steps.stepSummary: רב ספרא answers that since the Torah showed the rule is essential for slaughtering, it showed the same for all the עבודות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the Torah revealed it for slaughtering, it revealed it for the other services too.
steps.whatsHappening: The answer is that we do not need a new פסוק. What the Torah showed for slaughtering carries over to the other עבודות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reasoning is 'הואיל וגלי גלי': once the Torah revealed that intention matters for one עבודה, we assume it matters for all of them. Slaughtering is treated as an example that teaches about the whole process.

keyTerms.meaning: Since it was revealed in one place, it was revealed for the others too

phrases.english: Since it revealed, it revealed.
phrases.notes: He means: once the Torah showed this for slaughtering, it showed it for all the עבודות.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the other עבודות.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The rule for slaughtering extends to all the עבודות through 'הואיל וגלי גלי'.

steps.title: רב אשי rejects the 'revealed' reasoning
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says we do not use the reasoning 'הואיל וגלי גלי'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: We do not say 'since it revealed, it revealed.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי rejects the previous answer and refuses to stretch the slaughtering rule to the other עבודות by logic alone. This prepares for his own source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב אשי, a rule taught about slaughtering stays with slaughtering unless a פסוק says otherwise. So the other עבודות still need their own source.

keyTerms.meaning: We do not say; we do not accept this reasoning

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
We do not say "since it revealed, it revealed."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: הוֹאִיל וְגַלִּי גַּלִּי לָא אָמְרִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reasoning of the previous answer.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The use of 'הואיל וגלי גלי' to extend the rule to the other עבודות
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A rule taught about slaughtering cannot be carried over to other עבודות by logic alone.

steps.title: רב אשי's source: 'This is the law of the burnt offering'
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי brings the פסוק 'זאת התורה לעולה ולמנחה' as the source for the other עבודות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, how do we know it for the other services? As it is written: 'This is the law of the burnt offering and of the meal offering...'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a new source from a פסוק that lists all the offerings together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of logic, רב אשי uses a פסוק. The פסוק groups all the offerings together in one list, and that list becomes the basis for the rule about the other עבודות.

keyTerms.meaning: 'This is the law of the burnt offering and of the meal offering'; a פסוק that lists the offerings together
As it is written

phrases.english: Rather, from where do we derive it for the services?
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is part of the corrected wording.

phrases.english: As it is written: "This is the law
phrases.notes: ויקרא 7:37

phrases.english: of the burnt offering, and of the meal offering, etc."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies a פסוק in place of the rejected logic.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source for the other עבודות is the פסוק 'זאת התורה לעולה ולמנחה'.

steps.title: A ברייתא includes בכור, מעשר and פסח
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that 'their offerings' in the next פסוק refers to בכור, מעשר and פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it was taught in a ברייתא: 'On the day He commanded the children of Israel to bring their offerings' refers to the בכור, the מעשר and the פסח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא showing that the next פסוק adds בכור, מעשר and פסח to the list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list in 'זאת התורה' does not mention בכור, מעשר or פסח. The ברייתא reads 'קרבניהם' in the following פסוק as including them. That brings פסח into the group of offerings that רב אשי's source is talking about.

keyTerms.meaning: A firstborn animal brought as an offering
The animal tithe offering
'Their offerings'; the word that includes the offerings missing from the list

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the פסח is included among the offerings, so רב אשי's source can apply to it.

phrases.english: And it was taught in a baraita:
"On the day that He commanded the children of Israel
phrases.notes: ויקרא 7:38

phrases.english: to bring their offerings"
this is the firstborn, the tithe, and the Paschal offering;
phrases.notes: These three are not in the list in the פסוק before, so 'their offerings' brings them in.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתַנְיָא: בְּיוֹם צַוֹּתוֹ אֶת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a ברייתא that widens רב אשי's פסוק to include פסח.
steps.raayaObject: That פסח, בכור and מעשר are included with the offerings listed in 'זאת התורה'

steps.title: All offerings are compared to peace offerings: correct intention is a מצוה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says the פסוק compares all the קרבנות to שלמים. Just as by שלמים correct intention, both for the type of קרבן and for the owner, is required as a מצוה, the same is true for every קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse compared it to peace offerings. Just as with peace offerings we need correct intention as a מצוה, whether about changing the type of offering or changing the owner, so too with every offering, for both kinds of change, it is a מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא from step 28 goes on. It uses the comparison to שלמים to show that every קרבן should be brought with the right intention, as a מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שלמים have no special word showing that intention is a must, so for them correct intention is only a מצוה. Because the פסוק puts all the קרבנות together with שלמים, every קרבן gets at least this מצוה-level rule. This covers both kinds of wrong intention: the wrong type of קרבן and the wrong owner.

keyTerms.meaning: A comparison the Torah makes by placing two things together in one פסוק, so they share rules
Doing a עבודה with intention for a different type of קרבן
Doing a עבודה with intention for someone other than the real owner
As a מצוה: the right way to do it from the start, but not something that ruins the קרבן if missed

phrases.english: The verse compared it to peace offerings.
phrases.notes: 'It' means all the קרבנות listed in the פסוק together with the שלמים.

phrases.english: Just as with peace offerings,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין שִׁינּוּי קוֹדֶשׁ בֵּין שִׁינּוּי בְעָלִים,
phrases.english: whether a change of offering-type or a change of owner,
we require correct intention as a מצוה;
so too with every offering,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין שִׁינּוּי קוֹדֶשׁ בֵּין שִׁינּוּי בְעָלִים,
phrases.english: whether a change of offering-type or a change of owner,
it is required as a מצוה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא of step 28 by explaining what the comparison to שלמים teaches.
steps.raayaObject: That correct intention is a מצוה for every קרבן, for both שינוי קודש and שינוי בעלים
steps.raayaSupportSource: The הקש of all the קרבנות in the פסוק to שלמים

steps.title: The Paschal offering is like peace offerings: no difference between slaughter and the other rites
steps.stepSummary: The comparison to שלמים teaches more. By שלמים, slaughtering and the other עבודות are treated the same. So by פסח, where intention is essential for slaughtering, it is also essential for all the other עבודות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And 'like peace offerings': just as with peace offerings you did not separate slaughtering from the other rites regarding the מצוה, so too with the Paschal offering, do not separate slaughtering from the other rites regarding the rule that it is essential. (Because 'it is' is said about slaughtering, it teaches only that it is essential.)
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא uses the same comparison to answer the question of step 24 for the פסח. The 'must-have' intention rule spreads from slaughtering to all the עבודות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By פסח, the Torah already showed that intention is essential for slaughtering. The question was how we know this for the other עבודות. Since שלמים treat all the עבודות alike, the פסח, which is compared to them, must also treat all its עבודות alike. So the essential rule covers every עבודה of the פסח.

keyTerms.meaning: Essential: if it is missing, the קרבן is not valid as intended
Slaughtering the קרבן
The other עבודות: receiving the blood, carrying it, and sprinkling it
The קרבן פסח, the Paschal offering

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two rules. From שלמים we learn that a rule is the same for all the עבודות. For פסח the rule being spread is the 'essential' rule, not just the מצוה.

phrases.english: And it is like peace offerings;
just as with peace offerings,
between slaughtering and the other rites
you did not distinguish regarding the מצוה;
so too with the Paschal offering, do not distinguish
between slaughtering and the other rites regarding it being essential.
(Because 'it is' is said about slaughtering,
phrases.notes: These words are in round brackets, so the corrected wording leaves them out. Some versions have them and some don't.

phrases.english: it teaches only that it is essential.)

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same comparison to שלמים to spread the essential rule from slaughtering to all the עבודות of the פסח.
steps.raayaObject: That by פסח correct intention is essential for all the עבודות, not only slaughtering
steps.raayaSupportSource: The הקש of פסח to שלמים, where the עבודות are not treated differently
steps.whyThisMatters: This answers step 24's question for פסח using a פסוק-based comparison instead of the 'הואיל וגלי גלי' reasoning that רב אשי rejected.

steps.title: Then why is the word 'it is' needed?
steps.stepSummary: If the comparison to שלמים already teaches that intention is essential for the פסח, the גמרא asks what the word 'הוא' by פסח comes to teach.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then, why do I need 'it is'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the word 'הוא' in the פסוק of פסח is for. It seems extra, now that so much is learned from the comparison.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah does not waste words, so every word must teach something. If the פסח's rules come through the comparison, the extra word 'הוא' needs its own purpose. The next step gives that purpose.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need it? A question about a word or rule that seems extra
'It is': a word in the פסוק that shows a rule is essential

phrases.english: But then, why do I need 'it is'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the purpose of the word 'הוא' in light of the derivation in step 30.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the word 'הוא' by פסח teaches

steps.title: 'It is' teaches that intention is essential for the Paschal offering but not for the guilt offering
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains: by פסח, 'הוא' is written about slaughtering, so intention is essential. By אשם, 'הוא' is written only after burning the fats, and an אשם is valid even if its fats were never burned. So the 'הוא' by אשם does not make anything essential.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: With the Paschal offering, 'it is' is said about slaughtering, to show that it is essential. But with the guilt offering, 'it is' is said only after the burning of the fats, and the guilt offering itself is valid even if its fats were not burned.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא. 'הוא' by פסח shows that intention is essential there. 'הוא' by אשם cannot teach this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Where 'הוא' appears in the פסוק matters. By פסח it sits right on slaughtering, so it makes that essential. By אשם it comes after the burning of the fats, which is not even required for the אשם to be valid, so this 'הוא' cannot make anything essential.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא
The guilt offering
Burning the fats and certain parts of the קרבן on the מזבח
Valid

steps.whatToRemember: Every קרבן needs the right intention as a מצוה, learned from שלמים. For פסח it is essential in every עבודה. The 'הוא' by אשם does not make intention essential, because it comes after the burning, and the burning itself is not essential.

phrases.english: As it was taught in a baraita:
With the Paschal offering, 'it is' is said about slaughtering, to show it is essential;

phrases.english: and the guilt offering itself, if its fats were not burned, is valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּדְתַנְיָא נֶאֱמַר בְּפֶסַח הוּא בִּשְׁחִיטָה לְעַכֵּב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 31 by explaining what 'הוא' teaches, contrasting פסח with אשם.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'הוא' by פסח, written about slaughtering, makes intention essential. 'הוא' by אשם comes after the burning, which is not essential, so it makes nothing essential.

steps.title: What is the source for חטאת?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how we know that a חטאת offered with the wrong intention is פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: A חטאת: from where do we learn this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves from פסח to חטאת. It asks for the source that a חטאת becomes פסול when it is offered with the wrong intention.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה listed two קרבנות that become פסול when offered שלא לשמן: פסח and חטאת. The source for פסח was already explained, so now the גמרא needs a separate source for חטאת.

keyTerms.meaning: A sin offering
From where do we know it?
Not for its own sake, meaning with the wrong intention

phrases.english: A sin offering, from where do we derive it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: With the פסח finished, the גמרא opens the parallel question for חטאת.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that shows a חטאת must be offered for its own sake.

steps.title: The פסוק requires slaughtering for the sake of a חטאת
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says 'and slaughter it for a חטאת', which teaches that the שחיטה must be done for the sake of a חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And slaughter it for a sin offering.' This teaches that the slaughtering must be for the sake of a sin offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק. The word 'לחטאת' shows that the שחיטה has to be done for the sake of a חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק could have just said 'and slaughter it'. The added word 'לחטאת', 'for a sin offering', ties the act of שחיטה to the correct intention. This source covers only שחיטה, which leads straight into the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: Slaughtering the animal
For the sake of
As it is written

phrases.english: As it is written: “And slaughter it for a sin offering”
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:33

phrases.english: That the slaughter must be for the sake of a sin offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 33.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The words 'וְשָׁחַט אֹתָהּ לְחַטָּאת' show that the שחיטה of a חטאת must be done לשמה.

steps.title: What is the source for collecting the blood?
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק covers שחיטה. The גמרא asks for the source for קבלה, collecting the blood, and begins to bring a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: We found a source for slaughtering. From where do we learn collecting the blood? As it is written:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the פסוק only spoke about שחיטה, and asks where we learn that קבלה of a חטאת also needs the right intention. The word 'דכתיב' sets up the answer, and the פסוק itself comes in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A source for one עבודה does not automatically cover the others. So the גמרא looks for a separate source for each עבודה of the חטאת, beginning here with קבלה.

keyTerms.meaning: We have found
Collecting the blood in a כלי
